variation.original_summary: Lost Cities is a two-player card game of hidden hands and timing. Each turn a player plays a card to a rising single-colour expedition or discards it face-up, then draws from the deck or a discard pile. Started expeditions cost points, wagers multiply the result, and the higher total over three deals wins.

review.evidence: Simple policies all lose. Always discarding scores 0 and loses to any positive score. Always playing the lowest card opens every colour, takes the cost on each, and ends up negative. Always wagering early multiplies losses as well as gains. The first player has only a small edge, because the game ends the instant the deck runs out, which can cost the second player a turn.

Experienced players beat novices reliably over three deals. The skill lies in counting cards, deciding when to commit to a colour, denying discards the opponent wants, and controlling the pace of the deck. The draw adds variance within one deal.
A weak player can still score by opening one or two strong colours. A strong player keeps gaining from tracking the opponent's colours, sizing wagers, and running the deck out at the right time.
Hands and deck order are hidden. Players must infer the opponent's colours from what they play, discard and pick up, and plan which colours to commit to over many turns.
Scoring is pure arithmetic: the sum of numbers, minus a cost, times the wager multiplier, plus a length bonus.

It is turn-based and text-only, but it is too large to build. Five colours, three deals and per-colour columns and discard piles for each player exceed the attribute and round limits. The board of discard spaces has to become state. The earlier build attempt failed on blank discard fields and on a {hand} placeholder.

problems: P1: Five colours, three deals and about 44 turns per deal exceed the limits of 20 attributes and 40 rounds.
P2: The previous variation stored the discard row as four text fields that started as blank strings. Players were shown empty internal fields and the build failed.
P3: The previous variation put the hand into a prompt as a {hand} placeholder that the step cannot fill.
P4: Separate discard piles with buried cards that can be dug back up need a stack per colour. That is too much state for the engine.
P5: The game ends the instant the last card is drawn, so the second player can lose a turn. That is a seat edge, and it grows in a shortened single-deal game.
P6: With fewer cards per player, the original cost of 20 and the 8-card bonus would make almost every expedition lose points and the bonus unreachable, which pushes play toward discarding everything.
P7: The 'just discarded' restriction needs a bookkeeping value. If it is stored as a blank text field it reproduces P2.

variation.name: Lost Cities: Three Expeditions
variation.summary: A one-deal, three-colour Lost Cities for two players. Players hold hidden hands, build rising expeditions with wagers, and draw from a shared face-up discard row in which each colour shows at most one card. Both players always get equal turns.
variation.rules:
CARDS. There are 33 cards in 3 colours: Red (R), Blue (B) and Green (G). Each colour has number cards 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, written like R7 or B10, plus 2 wager cards, written RW, BW and GW (two of each).

SETUP. Shuffle all 33 cards into a face-down deck. This is the only random event in the game. Deal 6 cards to each player. Each player's hand is a hidden list that only its owner can see; the engine shows it to its owner as part of that player's state.

Table state:
- deck: hidden list, 21 cards remaining after the deal.
- discard_tops: public list of face-up cards, at most one per colour. It starts as an empty list.
- last_discard: hidden bookkeeping value, never shown to players. It starts as 'none'.

Player state, for each player and each colour c in R, B, G:
- sum_c: total of the numbers played in that colour. Starts at 0.
- top_c: highest number played in that colour, 0 meaning no number yet. Starts at 0.
- wag_c: number of wagers played in that colour. Starts at 0.
- cnt_c: number of cards in that colour's expedition, wagers included. Starts at 0.
- score: the player's current score. Starts at 0.
All player state is public except hand.

ROUND. Seat 1 is chosen at random. Each round, seat 1 takes a turn and then seat 2 takes a turn.

A TURN has two choices.

(1) PLAY OR DISCARD. The active player answers with one of:
- 'PLAY X', where X is a card in their hand.
- 'DISCARD X', where X is a card in their hand.

A PLAY is legal if:
- X is a number greater than top_c of its colour; or
- X is a wager and top_c of its colour is still 0.

When a play is legal, remove X from the hand, add 1 to cnt_c, then:
- for a number: add X to sum_c and set top_c to X;
- for a wager: add 1 to wag_c.

An illegal PLAY, or a card not in the hand, is treated as DISCARD of the first card in the hand.

A DISCARD removes X from the hand. If discard_tops already contains a card of X's colour, that old card is removed from the game permanently. Then X is appended to discard_tops, and last_discard is set to X.

(2) DRAW. The active player answers one of:
- 'DECK': take the top card of the deck into the hand.
- The name of a card in discard_tops other than last_discard: move that card from discard_tops into the hand.

An invalid answer, or naming last_discard, means DECK. If the deck is empty, the player must take a card from discard_tops other than last_discard. If none is available, the player draws nothing.

After the draw, last_discard is reset to 'none'. Both players always see discard_tops, both players' expedition numbers, and how many cards remain in the deck.

END OF ROUND. Recompute both scores. For each colour:
- if cnt_c = 0, the colour scores 0;
- otherwise it scores (sum_c - 15) x (1 + wag_c), plus 10 if cnt_c is 5 or more.
A player's score is the total of their three colours.

The game ends at the end of the round in which the deck became empty, or at the end of round 20, whichever comes first. Seat 2 always finishes the round, so both players take the same number of turns.
variation.objective: When the game ends, the player with the higher score wins. If the scores are equal, the game is a draw.
variation.expected_effect: Players must decide which of three colours to commit to, given a hidden hand and knowledge of which cards are already gone. They must judge whether to wager before seeing enough numbers, infer the opponent's colours from what they play and pick up, avoid discarding cards the opponent wants, and use discard pickups to slow the deck when they need more turns or draw from the deck to speed the end. Because columns cost 15 points, blind openings lose points, and always discarding scores 0, so neither simple policy is safe. Equal turn counts remove the seat edge. The deck order adds variance, but card counting and denial let the stronger player win most games. Talk is omitted because with two players and opposed interests it adds nothing to reason about. Build notes: there are no blank fields, since discard_tops is a list (possibly empty), last_discard uses the sentinel 'none' and is hidden as bookkeeping, and every counter starts at 0. Prompts use only {seat} and {value}; hands reach players through the hidden hand attribute.

balanced.evidence: PAYOFF TABLE for one colour, score = (sum - 15) x (1 + wag), plus 10 if cnt >= 5. No column = 0. {9,10}: sum 19, scores 4 / 8 / 12 with 0 / 1 / 2 wagers. {8,9,10}: 27, scores 12 / 24 / 36. {6..10}: 40, cnt 5, scores 25+10 = 35 / 50+10 = 60 / 75+10 = 85. {2,3,4}: 9, scores -6 / -12 / -18. A lone wager: -15 / -30 / -45. Each colour's numbers total 54. A player takes about 10-12 turns (21-card deck, longer if discards are drawn), so roughly 4-8 cards are played. That makes the 15-point threshold a real trade-off between starting a colour and waiting. No option dominates: wagers multiply losses as well as gains, and they must be played before any number. THOUGHTLESS POLICIES under the winner rule (higher score wins, equal is a draw). (a) Always DISCARD and draw DECK scores exactly 0. Any opponent who plays, for example, R8, R9, R10 scores 12 > 0, so it loses to sensible play. It draws only against an opponent who also scores exactly 0, and it can beat only an opponent who goes negative. It does not never-lose. (b) Always PLAY the first card: low cards like R2 are committed early and block better runs. Illegal plays become forced discards of the first card. Weak colours are started, often ending negative, so it loses to sensible play and roughly coin-flips against random play. (c) Always draw from the discard: this only stalls the deck toward the round-20 cap and gives no edge. (d) Play every wager immediately: a wager with no later 15+ number sum gives -30 to -45, so it loses heavily when its cards do not come. No policy never loses. SEAT: both seats take equal turns. Seat 1 makes the first commitment. Seat 2 may be forced to draw from discards on the last turn if the deck empties on seat 1's draw. Both effects are small, and seat 1 is assigned at random. Both players can win. This is not a cooperation game, so the 'safe option dominates' test does not apply.

playable.evidence: Every situation is defined: (1) legal and illegal plays (an illegal play becomes a discard of the first card in hand); (2) discard replacement (the old top is removed from the game); (3) drawing, with last_discard blocked and an invalid answer meaning DECK; (4) an empty deck (take a non-last discard, else draw nothing); (5) scoring; (6) the end, when the deck empties at round end or at round 20, with seat 2 finishing the round. FINITE: at most 20 rounds. ARITHMETIC: the result is calculated from public sum_c, wag_c and cnt_c. LIMITS: 2 choices per turn x 2 = 4 choice steps. Per turn there is choose, resolve play, resolve discard, choose draw and resolve draw, so 5 x 2 = 10 steps; adding 2 scoring calcs and 1 end check gives about 13 <= 20. ATTRIBUTES: 13 per-player + deck, discard_tops, last_discard and hand = 17 <= 20. HIDDEN ELEMENTS: deck, hands and last_discard = 3 <= 3, at the limit. RANDOM DRAWS: the shuffle happens at setup, so 0 per round. Rounds: 20 <= 40. No board, clock or judge is needed, and there is no trading or binding. Two players need no talk phase. MINOR ISSUES: the random seat choice contradicts 'the only random event'. 'First card in the hand' depends on list order, which the engine keeps by append order. Neither breaks play.

reasoning_over_luck.evidence: CHANCE: the deal and the deck order set which high cards and wagers each player sees. There is only one scoring round, against three in the original, so variance is notable. I estimate chance decides about 35-45% of games between equally competent players. DECISIONS THAT MATTER: (1) Holding low cards while committing to colours in increasing order: an early 7 kills 2-6. (2) Whether to start a colour, given the 15-point threshold and the 5-card +10 bonus. (3) Wager timing under uncertainty. (4) Discard denial: never discarding a card the opponent's open column needs. (5) Inferring the opponent's hand from their columns, their discard pickups and the shrinking deck, since each colour has only 9 numbers shared by both players. (6) Tempo: drawing discards to slow the deck, or drawing deck to rush the end while ahead. A careful player clearly beats random or thoughtless play. When both play well, the deal shifts outcomes, but the choices still change scores by tens of points, so the deal is not the sole decider. There is real hidden information (hands, deck) and a way to act on inferences (denial discards, draw choice).

triage.guidance:
Redefine the discard tops row so its 'empty' state is never a blank string. Either:
- give each discard_<colour> a non-empty sentinel such as 'none' (starts 'none'; 'none' = no face-up card), and say in the rules that drawing from a colour showing 'none' is an unavailable source (deck top instead), or
- replace the four text fields with a single public list attribute `discard_tops` that holds the face-up cards, which is empty when the row is cleared.
Keep everything else unchanged. Also note for the coder that prompts may only use the placeholders the step fills ({value}, {seat}), so a hand must reach players through a hidden hand attribute, not a {hand} placeholder.

triage.guidance:
1) Setup: give the table's `deck` attribute the 33-card list as its starting value, then shuffle and deal 6 to each hand. Do not append the cards to the deck in steps. That way a test that presets deck, hands or discard_tops is not overwritten or dealt into again. Keep `deck_size` in sync with the deck length after every draw.
2) Draw step: build draw_offer as 'DECK' (only while the deck is non-empty) plus every card in discard_tops except last_discard. Put these options to the active seat each turn.
3) Draw answers: an invalid answer, or naming last_discard, falls back to DECK. With an empty deck, allow only discard_tops cards other than last_discard. If there are none, the player draws nothing.
4) Reset last_discard to 'none' after each draw, so the other seat can pick up the card just discarded (for example, seat 2 taking seat 1's R9).
5) End the game at the end of the round in which deck_size reached 0, after seat 2 has finished its turn, or at round 20.

triage.reason: The rules say every draw is a choice the player answers: 'DECK' or the name of an eligible card in discard_tops. The game skips that choice whenever only one option is legal. DECK was never put to Ada when it was the only legal draw, and seat 2 silently 'took R9 from the discard row' without being offered it. Nothing here exceeds the platform; the file resolves the draw step automatically instead of polling.
triage.guidance:
Always pose the DRAW choice to the active player, even when only one option is legal.

Build the draw options like this:
- Include 'DECK' whenever deck_size > 0.
- Add every card in discard_tops except last_discard.
- When the deck is empty, offer only the discard_tops cards other than last_discard.
- Skip the draw, drawing nothing, only when that list is empty.

Do not auto-resolve a single-option draw by setting `take` directly; the player must be asked and the answer must be matched.

Handle answers as follows:
- An invalid answer, or the name of last_discard, falls back to DECK. Keep that fallback in the resolution step.
- Reset last_discard to 'none' after the draw.
- After the draw, set deck_size to the deck length.

Check that the scenario's given state is not overwritten by your setup/deal steps. The trace shows a fresh 33-card deal running, so make sure dealing happens only at game start.

triage.reason: The game is built correctly, but fixed one-option policies beat random play 85-95% of the time from either seat. The likely cause is the scoring: any expedition starts at -15 and wagers multiply losses, so a policy that never opens one (always discarding, or always repeating one kind of answer) sits near 0 while varied play usually goes negative.
triage.guidance: Rebalance so that refusing to commit is not the safe winning line, and keep the change simple. Possible changes: (1) Lower expedition_cost to about 5-8. With only about 10 plays per player in a 21-card deck, three colours at -15 each are almost impossible to recover. (2) Make wagers multiply only a positive colour total, e.g. score (sum_c - cost) x (1 + wag_c) when positive and (sum_c - cost) when negative, so one bad wager is not a disaster. (3) Penalise discarding, e.g. a player may not discard if they hold a legal play, or each discard costs 1 point, so endless discarding is not free. (4) Optionally add a small flat reward per card played, so opening expeditions has value from the start. The goal is that sensible card choices, such as playing low numbers before high and committing to colours you hold, beat both doing nothing and random play, with neither seat favoured.
